correctness.rationale: The standard order polytope is cut out by x_p>=0 for minimal p, x_p<=1 for maximal p, and x_q-x_p>=0 on covers; using the extra redundant coordinate bounds for all coordinates does not change containment. Facet-normal Euclidean norms are 1 and sqrt2. A radius-r ball obeys coordinate clearances and cover gaps sqrt2*r. Summing along a saturated longest chain from minimal to maximal yields (h-1)sqrt2*r<=1-2r, so r<=1/(2+(h-1)sqrt2). The lower-depth point L_p=r(1+sqrt2*d_-(p)) satisfies all margins, proving equality; backward-depth U likewise feasible. Every center lies L<=c<=U, and both are actual centers. Their equality is equivalent to d_-(p)+d_+(p)=h-1 for every p, i.e. longest chains cover P. Verified boundary cases including h=1 cube radius 1/2 and a 3-chain radius 1/(2+2sqrt2). Supplied 5231-poset checker is finite corroboration only.
residual_risks: Finite checker does not prove all posets; proof relies on correct normal lengths and the standard cover facet system.
